clinician.final_diagnosis: Inflammatory Myofibroblastic Tumor (IMT) of the cecum
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 68-year-old man presented with one month of colicky right lower quadrant pain radiating to the back, associated with 2-3 kg weight loss and anorexia. Initial CT imaging revealed a well-demarcated homogeneous solitary cecal mass with thickened ileum wall (E004). Colonoscopy demonstrated a large mass-like lesion in the cecum from which biopsies were obtained (E005). Histopathological examination of the biopsy specimen showed lamina propria infiltration by polymorphonuclear cells and eosinophils. Immunohistochemical staining was positive for vimentin, CD68, and focally positive for ALK, SMA, and CD34, while negative for CD117 (E006), a profile characteristic of IMT and excluding GIST. Following pathological confirmation of IMT (E008), the patient underwent surgical exploration revealing 40 mL ascites, cecal mass with ileocolic intussusception, and no enlarged lymph nodes. He underwent right hemicolectomy with end-to-end ileocolic anastomosis (E008). The patient was discharged seven days post-operatively without complications.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: CT scan demonstrated well-demarcated homogeneous solitary cecal mass with thickened ileum wall
Colonoscopy revealed large mass-like lesion in cecum with biopsy obtained
Histopathology showed inflammatory infiltrate (PMNCs, eosinophils) with IHC positive for vimentin, CD68, focal ALK, SMA, CD34 and negative for CD117
Pathological confirmation of IMT established leading to surgical referral
Surgical findings included cecal mass with ileocolic intussusception, 40 mL ascites, no enlarged lymph nodes; right hemicolectomy performed
Uneventful postoperative course with discharge on day 7 and no complications

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: CD117 (C-Kit) negativity on immunohistochemistry (E006) despite cecal mass location
Well-demarcated solitary mass on CT (E004) and mass-like lesion on colonoscopy (E005) rather than mucosal inflammation; specific IHC profile diagnostic of neoplastic process
